Syd James was first home in 56m. 15s. closely followed by Eric Hall, 56m.26s. with Brian Shepherd 3rd. and the match resulted in a win for us by 47 points to 89.
27 started and at half way Eric Hall, Syd James and A. McFarlane (Police) were in the lead, followed by Brian Shepherd, George Checkley, Bob Newson and Percy Wright.
Green, Syd James, Bob Newson, Brian Shepherd, McGreechan and Beecham. Crossing Purley Way, Syd had moved up to Eric and Evans with Bob coming along like a rocket.

George Beecham started to move up to split the Surrey pack, but they put on another spurt and began to move away again. In the meantime Syd James was away in the lead and won in 80m.21secs. with Eric 2nd.
At 4 miles Syd James was 15th, Eric Hall 18th, George Checkley 30th, Hugh McGreechan 36th and Bob Newson 40th. It was pleasing to see Bennard Eglington home from Germany and competing.
Syd James and Bob Newson were 3rd and 4th in 2hrs 13mins. 44secs and the "Demon-chest-King" 7th. The match, six a side, resulted in a win for us by 40 points to Surrey's 61, with the Police 81.
The first six Londoners were to be selected for a visit to Paris and competition was very keen with Syd James, Eric Hall, Bob Newson, George Checkley and George Beecham all in the field.

There was a total of 46 walkers from this country including six of our members, viz; George Place, Cyril Yescombe and Syd Spencer in the Police team and Ber[illegible]ard Eglington, Jack Goswell and myself in the R.W.A. team, with Sid James and Ron Kim as attendants.
We were unfortunate to suffer a disqualification in the 4 miles when Syd James failed to please the judges. This naturally pulled us back in the scoring, but even so we finished third to Metro.
Eric Hall was first home in 39mins. 6 secs. followed by Ted Smith, Syd James and Bob Newson and the match resulted in a win for us by 52 points to 119.

We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.

Ron West, a second claim member who was walking in the handicap which was held in conjunction, walked an exceptionall good race to beat Eric for first place. George Checkley, rapidly coming back to form was a good second, with Syd James 3rd.
Syd James and Hugh McGreechan finished together in 1h. 44m. and Len Demmon and Trevor Luck certainly walked well. Harry Shields, with an allowance of 12 minutes, won the handicap.
Eric Hall walked a very good race to win the individual title in 81m. 13secs. almost unchallenged and he was followed in 2nd place by Syd James, just over a minute behind.
George Checkley walked really well to win in 40m.12s. with Bob Newson second, Syd James (whom we are pleased to see out again) third and Eric Froude, still improving, fourth.

Our lads showed steady improvement and we were glad to see Dave McMullen and Syd James to the fore. Ted Smith was our first man home in (10th) followed by McMullen, Checkley and Newson, 12th, 15th and 16th.
Ted Smith,showing his true form,was 4th,Syd James 12th, Checkley 5th.McMullen 7th and Newson 13th.After this we can hope to regain the Berman Cup in our own Open on Nov24th.

Eric Hall retained his title, winning by 34 sec. from 2nd claim member George Williams who had travelled up from Worcester (that's enthusiasm). In the champioship Dave McMullen was 2nd and Syd James 3rd. Dave just pipped Williams for the handicap with Bob Readman a popular 3rd.
Packing well, our lads put their team in the first twelve positions with Ted Smith 7th, Dave McMullen 8th, George Checkley 9th, Syd James 11th and Bob Newson 12th!
We were without Syd James, and Dave McMullen was not at his best, owing to an attack of flu. First-class dressing accommodation was provided at a boy's school on the outskirts of Coventry.

Congratulations to Syd James and George Beecham on their recent marriages. Colin Collis is weakening; having bashed the Club '7' and run quite well he only needs a few well directed words and perhaps he'll be changing in the stable at Windsor Castle again in 1958.
Moreover most of our men reported fit and well, although we should have liked to have seen Bob Newson, Syd James and Roy Switzer in the field.

Syd James is back on the road again after a cartilage operation and a long spell off. He has got eight of his colleagues at work interested enough in walking to form a team for entry to the London Business Houses Championship.
The Handicap was won by evergreen Sid James off 10 Minutes.
Charlie was again selected as Team Captain for the County, the other three also being members of the team with Syd James as reserve, for the Inter Counties Championship at Leicester.
Another old walker still active is Syd James, former Surrey Champion. He is engaged in activities with the physically handicapped in his locality.
